segments: Tenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
al-Din Ali Kawshak (Kojek:
Kokburi?), the lord of Erbil.
And Saladin introduced into Acre skilled men who were fire-throwers,
and they burned three large siege-towers (belfries) of the Franks.
And God helped the Franks,
for the wind was blowing towards the city;
otherwise most of them would have burned in that fierce blaze of the siege-towers,
because the trench which they had dug behind them
prevented them from fleeing before the fiery flames.
For onto carts they had mounted these siege-towers,
and when they wished, they pushed them with lances and brought them close to the wall,
with their warriors inside them;
and when they wished,
they pulled them towards themselves with ropes.
An action that astonished and terrified onlookers.
Now the king of the Germans, when he came out to Constantinople,
the Greeks tried to stop him.
And when he fought and defeated {OCR?} them,
they submitted to him,
and granted him passage,
and he crossed over and came to the territory of Qilij Arslan.
And Qutb al-Din Malik-Shah, the son of the Sultan, gathered an army of Turcomans,
and they encountered the Germans,
and the Turcomans were defeated and fled.
And the Germans came and entered the city of Iconium,
and they killed many in it.
And at that time,
Papa (Papas?) Michael, a Greek priest and notary from Melitene,
who had gone to render an account,
was killed there.
Now Qilij Arslan, the Sultan, took refuge in the fortress of Iconium,
and afterwards he gave gifts to the king of the Germans,
and made peace,
and granted him passage;
and he crossed over into the territory of Cilicia.
And Leo, the son of Stephen, the son of Leo, the ruler of Cilicia, came to him at Tarsus,
and showed fair submission.
And when that old king of the Germans stood in the river to bathe—
and there was intense cold on that day—
he became ill and died there,
and his son carried his body to Antioch.
And from there the Germans went towards Tripoli;
and because they were exhausted from the toil of the journey,
they boarded ships and only a few men went forth to Acre,
because most of them had died of sickness in Cilicia.
[Note:] He drowned while crossing the river.
In June 1190 {OCR: 1100} of our Lord.
